label: EXISTENCE_IN_ESSENCE_5: some essential truth of x entails its existence (consequential form)
definition: NatureEntailsExistence F Essential x := ∃ φ, EssentialTruth Essential x φ ∧ EntailsExistence F φ x: some proposition that lies in the nature of x (ESSENCE_5) holds only at points where x exists. Weaker than EXISTENCE_IN_ESSENCE_2 (EssentialExistence implies it).
note: Stipulated for #1887. Sense EXISTENCE_IN_ESSENCE_5 of the disambiguation f704b7ca-b455-4da7-a757-b0564fe76b3b. Its denial for x is exactly what existence-conditional essences yield once x's absence is representable (ModalGrounding controls, law 4), and what Kant's thesis with concept adequacy yields for every being (controls of docs/notes/existence-in-essence-identity.md, law 2). Within the essentialist framework it is equivalent to x's necessity for an actual x (same controls, law 11).
